tier_reason: Peer-reviewed ICML 2025 paper (linked from the repo README) reports kernel speedups over e3nn and NVIDIA cuEquivariance; the abstract numbers (up to 41.6x and 60.8x; SevenNet-l3i5 4.2x/3.5x speed, 6.3x/6.2x memory) appear identically in WebSearch snippets of openreview and proceedings.mlr.press. The paper itself was EGRESS_BLOCKED, so GPU model and flags could not be checked and the repo README carries no numbers, which rules out A.

corrections.caveats: Paper (openreview, proceedings.mlr.press, mlanthology) EGRESS_BLOCKED; numbers are from WebSearch snippets of the ICML 2025 abstract only, so GPU model, precision and the configuration on which the 41.6x/60.8x maxima occur are unverified. The 'up to' figures are maxima, and the per-phase figures (forward/backward/double-backward) were not confirmed. Repo README gives no numbers; it ships microbenchmarks (example/test.sh runs example/flashTP_test.py over ir_config/) that a user can rerun; the build auto-detects GPU compute capability and falls back to sm_80/sm_90 with PTX. Scope is the channelwise 'uvu' tensor product only (drop-in for e3nn.o3.TensorProduct uvu). Baselines are Python/PyTorch e3nn (with torch_scatter) and cuEquivariance, not a C++ default. No head-to-head against OpenEquivariance in the paper per the OpenEquivariance issue #171 remark; Sobek lists FlashTP only as a related library.

corrections.caveats: The paper (arxiv.org abs/html/pdf, pith.science) was EGRESS_BLOCKED, so the numbers are from WebSearch snippets of the abstract and could not be checked against tables; GPU model and per-case numbers unknown. Repo ships a benchmark CLI (suites minimal, scaling, throughput, uvu-throughput; 'matched' command for OpenEquivariance-capacity-matched timing; peak-memory re-measurement with --memory-only) but no checked-in results and no paper PDF (tree: sobek/, tests/, LICENSE, NOTICE, pyproject.toml). Speedups are over a partly different formulation (Sobek fuses the final radial projection while baselines take precomputed per-edge weights), and comparisons are capacity-matched against OpenEquivariance, so 1.2x-49.7x is a range over cases, not a typical figure. Float32 only. No evidence of a benchmark against FlashTP (README only lists FlashTP among related libraries). Very young repo: 5 commits between 2026-07-20 and 2026-07-24, 12 stars, 0 forks.

tier_reason: The README table numbers are real (bench.cpp, Google Benchmark, CMake Release on i7-1185G7), but neither the README nor bench.cpp runs any baseline: no JS Flatbush, Boost.Geometry, CGAL, GEOS or nanoflann. The only comparison is reading two README tables measured on different CPUs and OSes with partly different search mixes, which measures no speedup, and on the one matching kNN row (1 search of 1,000,000 neighbors) the C++ gcc/clang figures (86/88ms on i7-1185G7) are not faster than JS (84ms on M1 Pro), so the claim is directional only.

corrections.claimed_speedup: No speedup claim on the page. C++ README table (i7-1185G7, bench.cpp): index 1000000 rectangles 55ms (clang 18.1.3), 59ms (gcc 13.3.0), 72ms (cl 19.29); 1000 searches 10%: 79/80/91ms; 1000 searches 1%: 17/18/18ms; 1 search of 1000000 neighbors: 88/86/63ms. JS original README (M1 Pro, Node v24): index 1,000,000 rectangles 109ms; 100 searches 10% area 64ms; 1000 searches 1% area 66ms; 1 search of 1,000,000 neighbors 84ms. Cross-CPU ratios (derived from page data, not like-for-like): index build 109/55 = about 2.0x; 1000 searches 1% about 3.7x (66/18); 1M-neighbor kNN about 1.0x or slower with gcc/clang.
corrections.compiler_and_flags: clang 18.1.3, gcc 13.3.0, cl 19.29.30159; CMake WITH_BENCHMARKS forces CMAKE_BUILD_TYPE Release (CMake defaults, explicit -O/-march flags not stated in the README); SIMD level used for the table not stated (SSE2 default on x64, AVX/AVX2/AVX512 selectable); bench uses Google Benchmark fetched at build time
corrections.caveats: No head-to-head against any baseline: bench.cpp benchmarks only this library (BM_Index1M, BM_Search10Percent, BM_Search1Percent, BM_Search001Percent, BM_Neighbors100, BM_NeighborsAll, BM_Neighbors1). The only cross-implementation comparison is derived by reading two README tables measured on different CPUs and OSes (i7-1185G7 vs Apple M1 Pro), and the JS table uses a different search mix (100 searches at 10% vs 1000), so it is directional; the matching 1M-neighbor kNN row shows no win for gcc/clang. Author says benchmarks are based on the original bench to allow a close comparison. A search snippet of the project page shows older numbers (93ms clang 10.0.0), so the tables were rerun over time; per-commit runner history is on chusitoo.github.io (blocked here). No comparison with Boost.Geometry rtree, CGAL, GEOS or nanoflann. C++ port of mourner/flatbush (ISC), which is already in the catalog; the port itself is MIT.
